reflections.title: "I will be an enemy to your enemies"

reflect.text: God promises that when we listen carefully to His guidance and obey Him, He takes our side completely. He sends His messenger before us to prepare our path. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, God enters into "a league with His people, offensive and defensive." When we stand for God and what is right, His cause becomes our cause. We do not need to carry fear about who opposes us, because God Himself takes up our battle and protects us.

Because God is our defender, we do not have to fight for our own pride or hold grudges. F. B. Meyer reminds us never to strike back or harbor hatred toward those who oppose us. Instead, we can feel compassion for them and pray for them, knowing how unhappy envy and bitterness make a person. When we walk in simple, quiet obedience to God's word, we can rest peacefully. He stands between us and harm, and He will safely vindicate His people.

questions: Are there situations where you are tempted to take revenge instead of letting God defend you?
How can praying for those who oppose you change the way you see them?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for promising to go before us and protect us when we follow Your voice. Help us to obey You completely and to leave all our battles in Your hands. Give us loving hearts that pray for those who oppose us instead of returning evil for evil. Amen.

reflections.title: God Prepares the Way for His People

reflect.text: As God leads His people toward the place He has prepared, He provides help for every step of the journey. Often, God sends help through the ordinary people around us. Just as friends bring food or lend a steady hand when someone is recovering from illness, God uses everyday helpers as His messengers of care. In the same way, He calls us to notice people in need and serve as His helping hands.

Serving God brings joy and fills our daily lives with His goodness. In Exodus 23:25, God promises to bless our simple bread and water. Even when we have only the most basic meals, God's grace, which is His unearned kindness, rests upon our table. As Charles Spurgeon observed, "our commonest things become blessed when we ourselves are consecrated to the Lord." Everything we receive from His hand becomes a gift of His love.

God also goes ahead of us to clear obstacles in ways we could never imagine. He promised Israel that He would send hornets to drive away their foes before the battle even began. God does not need our strength to clear the path. His unexpected methods can do far more than our own efforts ever could. We simply need to trust His leading and move forward, knowing He is already working ahead of us.

questions: How has God used ordinary people to help and encourage you during hard times?
In what simple parts of your daily life can you pause to thank God for His blessing?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for providing for our needs and clearing our path in ways we cannot foresee. Thank You for the people You send to support us and for blessing our daily bread. Show us how we can be Your helping hands to others who need care today. Amen.
